review.issue: Idea 2's title uses the word 'bowls', which suggests eating/drinking ware; the source explicitly excludes objects used for eating or drinking, so using 'bowls' risks implying the event accepts those items.
review.sourceEvidence: The team will look at decorative ceramics such as vases and figurines. It will not accept objects used for eating or drinking, because its adhesives are not certified for food contact.

review.issue: The draft language states the taster 'reduces uncertainty about attending' as an effect. The source records the organisers' intent (to help a hesitant newcomer picture the evening and decide whether to come) but does not provide evidence that the notice actually reduces newcomer uncertainty or changes behaviour; change wording to reflect intent rather than proven effect.
review.sourceEvidence: The notice is intended to help a hesitant newcomer picture the evening and decide whether to come.

review.issue: The draft treats rehearsal feedback as supporting narrative claims without noting sample size or that responses are descriptive rather than causal. The source gives counts from 12 respondents and explicitly notes there has been no survey or comparison, so the draft should keep the use of the feedback but add the sample/limitation context.
review.sourceEvidence: After the October rehearsal, twelve of the nineteen people present answered a short question about returning. Eight mentioned the welcome, three mentioned the songs, and one mentioned both. Two people who had missed the previous rehearsal said late trains had played a part. The choir agreed at its monthly meeting to keep the later entry window through December. The minutes record the decision without an account of why it was chosen. There has been no survey of confidence before and after singing and no comparison with a fixed-start rehearsal.

review.issue: The draft's rationale for the first idea asserts that an expectation‑setting piece is 'likely to address the main barrier signalled in the source,' which reads as a causal claim. The source reports that 'welcome' was the most‑cited return reason and that the committee kept a later entry window, but it does not provide evidence that an expectation‑setting notice will reduce hesitation or increase attendance.

review.issue: The draft adds role-specific readers ('senior managers and decision-makers') to the audience for the onboarding brief; the source only identifies 'other member housing associations considering participation' without naming roles.
review.sourceEvidence: Its introductory note is addressed to other member housing associations considering participation.

review.issue: Idea 2's audience names 'operations leads' in addition to caretakers and repairers; the source documents caretakers and the inventory's use by a repairer but does not mention operations leads.
review.sourceEvidence: Two caretakers have entered sample items in a shared inventory. That inventory is intended to help a repairer locate an item and see its fabric and dimensions.

review.issue: Idea 3's audience specifies 'Leadership teams and boards of housing associations' while the source only indicates that member associations will review pilot work and does not explicitly name boards or the exact leadership roles.
review.sourceEvidence: Members will review the initial work before considering upholstery or other textile services.

review.issue: Idea 3's description refers to 'trade-offs of committing staff time or stock', but the source does not mention staff time or stock commitments; that phrase is not supported by the provided source.
review.sourceEvidence: No price list, savings estimate or turnaround promise has been agreed. Members will review the initial work before considering upholstery or other textile services.

review.issue: The draft names 'UX/designers charged with the site navigation' as an explicit audience; the source identifies local reading groups as invitees but does not mention UX or design staff as intended recipients of the pilot.
review.sourceEvidence: Thirty invitation links were sent to local reading groups.

review.issue: The funder-facing memo description in the draft says it will 'outline ... estimated resource needs' for full translations; the source states further translations are possibilities for a later funding application but does not provide or imply cost estimates in the published account.
review.sourceEvidence: Further languages and full translated chapters remain possibilities for a later funding application, rather than promised additions.

review.issue: The reader-facing primer in the draft promises an FAQ addressing 'the most common confusions reported in the pilot.' The source records four comments about navigation but does not characterize them as 'most common' or provide a broader set of reported confusions.
review.sourceEvidence: So far nine people have opened the feedback form, and four have submitted comments about finding their way between summaries and interviews.
